abstract: Is the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) going to degrade management knowledge? In their point essay, Nolan, Lindebaum, and Ashraf (2026) (NLA hereafter) argue that LLMs will unavoidably degrade knowledge production in management and organization studies—eroding deep reading, dissuading scholars from the real world, diminishing collegial engagement, and homogenizing scholarly output. In our counterpoint essay, we argue that this dire diagnosis undeservedly pathologizes a technology for the problems created by systemic shortcomings that predate its advent, and it erroneously infers the degradation of knowledge from individual misuse since the corpus of knowledge is decided by system-level factors. Rather than stigmatizing the use of LLMs, we maintain that our focus should be on addressing preexisting pathologies that the technology is only making more pressing—chiefly about the effectiveness of our filtering systems. We also show that in capturing only reinforcing loops, NLA’s deterministic model fails to acknowledge (1) the positive dynamics associated with the productive use of the technology and (2) the balancing dynamics of second-order effects—scarcity premiums and sharpened gatekeeping. Finally, we challenge widespread philosophical assumptions underpinning NLA’s anti-LLM skepticism, explaining that they rest on the reification of meaning and an anthropomorphic conception of intelligence.

ob.tldr: 反驳大语言模型必然损害管理知识的观点：知识退化并非源于个体误用，而更多受既有制度缺陷和筛选机制制约；仅关注强化回路还会忽视生产性使用、稀缺溢价及把关收紧等二阶效应，主张治理系统性问题而非污名化LLM。

title: Complex analyses for complex problems: Beyond the pathologization of Generative AI and the stigmatization of its use
